notes.name: r1-note1
notes.notes: 45-year-old man presents with right knee pain for three weeks after a fall. He has hypertension and takes lisinopril 10 mg daily. Allergies: penicillin. Smoker: No. On examination there is a small effusion and medial joint line tenderness. Assessment is a probable medial meniscus tear. Plan is an MRI of the right knee and physiotherapy referral.

notes.name: r1-note2
notes.notes:
Patient presents with a cough for five days.
She reports low-grade fevers and green sputum.
She has asthma.
Medications: salbutamol inhaler as needed.
Allergies: none known.
Smoker: no.
Chest examination revealed crackles at the right base.
Assessment: community-acquired pneumonia.
Plan: amoxicillin 500 mg three times daily for five days.
Return if symptoms worsen.

notes.name: r1-note4
notes.notes: This is a 30-year-old female seen for headaches. The headaches started two months ago and are worse in the morning. She denies visual changes, nausea, or weakness. She takes ibuprofen as needed. No known drug allergies. She is a nonsmoker. Neurological examination is normal. Assessment is tension-type headache. Plan is to start amitriptyline 10 mg at night. She will follow up in six weeks.
